blocks.title: The rules and the argument, year by year

label.text: dated meetings in the record below
of them heard only in our machine captions

so.text: Those mark where something was said; the minutes, where they exist, are what the town recorded.

claims.text: 5 of the 18 dated meetings here are known only from our machine captions.

note.text: A row drawn apart rests on our machine captions alone: a caption locates a moment, and no figure heard in one is given here.

why.text: Board of Selectmen, 15 January 2013 (minutes): Lists the Town's financial management policies as adopted by the Board of Selectmen in July 2004.
Finance Committee, 21 August 2014 (minutes): Votes 4-0 to recommend that the Board of Selectmen approve the financial policies the committee drafted.
Board of Selectmen, 2 September 2014 (minutes): Votes 5-0 to adopt them. The summary says rating agencies rate the Town more favorably with a healthy stabilization balance and policies it follows.
Board of Selectmen, 2 January 2018 (minutes): Approves the OPEB funding policy as amended, subject to the Finance Committee: at least 10% of certified free cash to the trust each year.
Finance Committee, 23 August 2018 (minutes): Votes 6-0 to recommend a change to the free cash policy.

Finance Committee and Board of Selectmen, 11 October 2018 (our machine captions only): Roads come off the free cash priority list, as paving had moved into the operating budget; the OPEB share takes their place. No minutes are held.
Select Board, 18 June 2024 (minutes): Introduces the draft financial policies written by the Division of Local Services under a Community Compact grant. No action is taken.
Finance Committee, 12 September 2024 (our machine captions only): Says local receipts have been estimated well below what was collected. The figures are heard in captions only.
Finance Committee, 27 February 2025 (our machine captions only): Says the Select Board has looked at the new financial policies but they have not been ratified.

Finance Committee, 3 April 2025 (minutes): Votes 6-0 to take no action on free cash to general stabilization, and 6-0 on free cash to the special purpose fund. In public comment, the reserve fund is called an account for emergencies, not a piggy bank.
Select Board, 16 December 2025 (minutes): Reports unassigned fund balance of about 18% of the budget, up from 17%.
Select Board, 16 March 2026 (minutes): Cautions that as budgets move closer to actual spending, less free cash will be generated.

rows.label: A resident and the Town Manager, 14 April 2026

why.text: Select Board, 14 April 2026 (minutes, part in captions only): A resident questions adding to reserves while schools face cuts. The Town Manager says funding operations from free cash is contrary to Town policy and state guidance.
Finance Committee, 28 May 2026 (minutes, part in captions only): Says local receipts have not come in under $4 million in ten years. A larger reserve fund is also raised, in captions only.
Select Board, 14 July 2026 (minutes): Proposes a goal of adopting four policies by December: OPEB, stabilization and reserves, free cash, and revenue projections.
Finance Committee, 22 October 2026 (our machine captions only): In public comment, calls the capital planning process unwieldy and undemocratic.
Select Board, 24 November 2026 (our machine captions only): Says the financial policy review is behind schedule; a state workshop on it had a poor response in scheduling.
Finance Committee, 3 December 2026 (the agenda): Lists a workshop to review financial policies for a recommendation to the Select Board, with 22 policy titles and no text attached.

so.text: Arguments on both dials have been made for years; the draft has been before the boards since June 2024 without a vote on it.

finding.text: The town’s financial policies date from 2014; the state’s replacement draft has waited since June 2024.
